_note: Advanced V2 concept questions for prefix-sums.

questions.title: Prefix meaning
choices: The sum before or through position i, depending on the convention
The original value at i only
The number of arrays in memory
questions.explanation: A prefix array stores totals from the start up to a chosen boundary. The boundary convention matters because every range subtraction depends on using the same indexing rule.

questions.title: Range formula
questions.prompt: Using prefix where prefix[0]=0 and prefix[i+1] is the sum through i, how do you get sum left..right?
questions.explanation: The total before left includes values you do not want. Subtracting it from the total through right leaves exactly the values from left through right.

questions.title: Empty prefix
questions.prompt: Why start some prefix arrays with a leading 0?
choices: It makes ranges starting at index 0 use the same formula
It stores the final answer twice
questions.explanation: The leading 0 represents the sum before the array begins, so left=0 does not need a special case.

questions.title: Index mistake
questions.prompt: What usually causes prefix-sum off-by-one bugs?
choices: Mixing inclusive and exclusive index conventions
questions.explanation: The formula is simple only when the meaning of each prefix index stays consistent.

questions.title: Many queries
questions.prompt: When are prefix sums especially useful?
choices: Many range-sum queries on data that is not changing
questions.explanation: Prefix sums move the repeated work to the setup step. After the totals are built once, each range query can be answered with one subtraction.

questions.title: Grid prefix
questions.prompt: What extra issue appears in a 2D prefix sum?
choices: Overlapping rectangle area must be added back once
questions.explanation: The top-left overlap is subtracted twice when removing top and left areas, so it must be added back.

questions.title: Negative values
questions.prompt: Can prefix sums work when numbers are negative?
choices: Yes, running totals still preserve range differences
questions.explanation: The subtraction formula still works because each prefix total includes the same earlier negative values consistently.

questions.title: Prefix mistake
questions.prompt: A range sum from index 2 to 4 is wrong by one item. What should be checked first?
choices: Whether right is inclusive or exclusive in the formula
Whether the code uses a heap
questions.explanation: Most range errors come from including one endpoint too many or too few. Check the prefix convention, then trace the left and right indexes against a tiny range.
